title: Fourier expansion of the product noise operator
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, correlation parameter $\rho\in[0,1]$, function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and input $x\in\Omega^n$, the product noise operator applied to $f$ at $x$ equals $\sum_a \rho^{|\operatorname{supp}(a)|}\widehat f(a)\,\phi_a(x)$, where the sum ranges over all multi-indices, $\operatorname{supp}(a)$ is the set of coordinates where $a$ is not the distinguished constant-basis index, $\widehat f(a)$ is the corresponding Fourier coefficient, and $\phi_a$ is the corresponding product basis function.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$B$ is a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ containing the constant-one function
